main_text.p: ad obsequium crucis, & redemptionem humani generis. Adeò hæc perspicua & aperta, ut Bellarmini aliorumque stupo-rem, stupere satis non possimus. Nemini ergo accidat mirum, scribentem ad Hebræos Apostolum, Græcorum uti versio-ne. Siquidem 1. Græco scriberet idiomate. II. Græcæ versioni lucem sæpius inferret. III. Ad scopum illa suum esset quàm ac-commodata. IV. Res ipsi cum Hebræis ἁρμόζοι, maximâ ex parte esset. V. Magno apud hos translatio esset in pretio, atque etiam usu. VI. Ipsi Hebræi illorum tempo-rum scriptores, Josephus, Philo, pariter usurparint. VII. Verbis etiam illa transla-tio, minimè sensu ab Hebræis codicibus discederet. VIII. Mos etiam Pauli esset Apostoli, suis passim in Epistoliis eâdem uti. Patet vel ex Epistolis ad Romanos, Galatas, in quibus cum ipsis disputat sæ-pè Judæis.
main_text.head: XVI. Undecimò, nec inepta, ut videtur Bellarmino, illa ratio est, quæque imprimis fuit Cajetani, ex Capite VII. versu 2. Quod sc. Author hebræam vo-cem

page.notes: Printed page numbers and roman numerals in the text (I–VIII) are as printed; the list numbers are set in small type. The line "XVI. Undecimò..." is a numbered paragraph, so it is kept as a paragraph, not a heading; the opening "XVI." is a bare number and I have kept it inside the paragraph text. Doubtful readings: "ἁρμόζοι" (Greek word in the Hebrew sentence, partly illegible on scan); "Epistoliis" as printed. The last line "cem" is a catchword-like continuation at the right foot and is printed on the page as the word that continues on the next page; it is transcribed in the text above as "vocem" continued on the next line.
